# All rules

## NR-01: Private dev packages use version 0.0.0 `[HOLD]`

> Every private development package named `…-dev` sets `"version": "0.0.0"`.

Old number: 1.2.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check names`

Issues: I-03.

This applies to manifest kinds
`dev`, `shared-helper`, and `internal-consumer`. Nothing resolves these packages by a published release range — a
workspace member links them by name — so any other number is a claim nobody verifies and everybody has to keep in
step with a release that does not exist. `fhevm-npm check names` enforces this fixed version together with the private
development naming boundary.

<a id="nr-02"></a>

## NR-02: Members are explicit paths, never globs `[GAP]`

> Every installation root lists its members as explicit relative paths, never globs.

Old number: 2.1.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check workspaces`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: add `"workspaces": ["*"]` to a standalone project with its own lockfile, e.g. ./hardhat/v3/plugin/test-consumer/esm/package.json: it becomes an installation root with a glob, and no check reads its workspaces field (package-json policy for standalone excludes nothing). Fix: issue I-70.

Issues: I-01, I-70.

The policy never records a concrete workspace-member list. That is changing inventory data and belongs in
`npm-manifest.json` and the root `package.json`. The central validator derives the expected `workspaces` array from
every non-root manifest entry whose `member` is `true`, removes the leading `./` from each key, and requires exact set
equality with the root array. Adding or removing a package therefore changes inventory, not this policy.

```text
expected workspaces = manifest package keys where member is true, with "./" removed
actual workspaces   = sdk/package.json#workspaces

✅ both sets are equal
❌ either set contains a path absent from the other
```

A member
is a package in the `workspaces` array of a root's `package.json`: npm links it to the other members of that
root and installs them together. A glob silently absorbs a new directory into the workspace, changing
resolution for every package under it before anyone reviews the change.

```jsonc
// ✅ Every member spelled out, so adding a directory is a reviewed edit.
"workspaces": ["packages/dev-owner", "packages/shared-helper"]

// ❌ Also swallows every matching directory added later.
"workspaces": ["packages/*"]
```

<a id="nr-03"></a>

## NR-03: The published payload lives in pkg/ `[GAP]`

> A dev owner stores its published payload in `pkg/`.

Old number: 2.1.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check ownership`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: set host-contracts-cleartext/v14/package.json "pack:tarball": "npm pack" (the rule's own counter-example): check scripts passes because only presence is checked. Fix: issue I-71.

Issues: I-71.

The dev-owner root is private and holds scripts, config
and tests; `pkg/` holds only what ships. Packing the dev-owner root publishes the development package by mistake.
In particular, a `published` package never declares `forge:fmt` or `forge:lint`, including when it is mirror-only:
the Forge scripts and `foundry.toml` belong to the corresponding `dev` owner.

```jsonc
// ✅ Delegates to the manifest-aware CLI: the payload comes from this owner's publishedRelPath, and
//    the tarball lands in npm-manifest.json#tarballs.relPath.
"pack:tarball": "node ../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts publish pack ./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>"

// ❌ Packs the member root, so foundry.toml, tests and internal/ all ship.
"pack:tarball": "npm pack"
```

<a id="nr-04"></a>

## NR-04: One member per published name `[GAP]`

> At most one workspace member has a given published package name, across every installation root.

Old number: 2.1.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check workspaces`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/workspaces.ts:81-105` groups by installation root and name, so two roots could each hold a member with the same name and pass. Fix: group by name only.

Issues: I-01, I-72.

When generations share a name, only the active generation's payload sets `member: true`; the validator groups
published entries by the `name` read from their real `package.json` and rejects a group with two member entries.
Which generation is active is inventory data.

```text
✅ Two generations share one name, and only the active one is a member:
   host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg     @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext   member: true
   host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg   @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext   member: false

❌ Two members share one name:
   host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg     @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext   member: true
   host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg   @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext   member: true
```

## NR-05: A standalone consumer is never a member `[HOLD]`

> A standalone consumer is never a member.

Old number: 2.1.4.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check workspaces`

Issues: I-08.

A project deliberately installed in place with its own
`package-lock.json` breaks the moment npm folds it into the root lockfile. A manifest-selected consumer copied outside
the workspace is a separate case covered by [NR-64](../entries/NR-64.md); its source may remain a member.

```jsonc
// ✅ Stable kind invariant; no concrete package path belongs in this rule.
{ "kind": "standalone", "member": false }

// ❌ Its own lockfile stops being authoritative after the root absorbs it.
{ "kind": "standalone", "member": true }
```

## NR-06: Every tsconfig path exists `[GAP]`

> Every literal local path named by an owned tsconfig exists.

Old number: 2.1.5.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check tsconfig-paths`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: ownedTsconfigs reads the `.` root's own folder without recursion and then only members and non-packages (tsconfig-paths.ts:114-116). A tsconfig directly in a cluster root, for example hardhat/v3/tsconfig.json with `"include": ["./deleted"]`, is skipped (kind workspace-root, member=false); so is a tsconfig in a root-owned subfolder such as scripts/tsconfig.json. fhevm-npm/tsconfig.json is outside the inventory and is not read either. Fix: issue I-73.

Issues: I-73.

`include`, `exclude`, `files`,
`references[].path` and relative `extends` entries are checked in root, member and non-package tsconfigs; globs are
not literal claims, and conventional transient-output names (`node_modules`, `out`, `cache`, …) may be absent.

```jsonc
// ✅ Existing source path and a glob that may currently match nothing.
{ "include": ["./src", "./generated/**/*.ts"] }

// ❌ A deleted literal path silently weakens TypeScript's coverage.
{ "exclude": ["./test/deleted-file.ts"] }
```

<a id="nr-07"></a>

## NR-07: Every entry point target exists `[GAP]`

> Every local entrypoint target in an inventoried `package.json` exists.

Old number: 2.1.6.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check package-json-paths`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: An exports target './package.json/x*' passes inspectPackageJsonPaths because dirname(prefix) is './package.json' and existsSync accepts this regular file. Reproduced without writing any files. Fix: issue I-74.

Issues: I-45, I-74.

The validator checks `main`, `module`,
`types`, `typings`, and every local leaf below `exports` and `imports`. An exact target must exist; for a target with
`*` or `?`, its non-wildcard directory must exist. External package targets below `imports` are not filesystem paths.

```jsonc
// ✅ Exact files exist, and the wildcard's directory exists.
{ "types": "./_types/index.d.ts", "exports": { "./abi/*": "./abi/*" } }

// ❌ The package advertises a file or directory that is absent.
{ "main": "./missing/index.js", "exports": { "./feature/*": "./missing/*" } }
```

## NR-08: Declare the module type explicitly `[HOLD]`

> Every package.json declares its module type explicitly.

Old number: 2.1.7.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check package-json`

Every manifest package sets `type` to either
`module` or `commonjs`; Node's implicit CommonJS default is not accepted.

```jsonc
// ✅ Explicit consumer runtime semantics.
{ "type": "commonjs" } // test-consumer/cjs/package.json
{ "type": "module" } // test-consumer/esm/package.json

// ❌ Runtime semantics depend on Node's default or contradict the fixture path.
{} // test-consumer/cjs/package.json
{ "type": "commonjs" } // test-consumer/esm/package.json
```

## NR-09: Published metadata follows the central field list `[GAP]`

> Published package metadata follows the central field list.

Old number: 2.1.8.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check package-json`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: delete "private" from npm-manifest.json#packageJson.published.excluded and add "private": false to host-contracts-cleartext/v14/pkg/package.json: every check passes. Fix: issue I-75.

Issues: I-75.

`npm-manifest.json#packageJson` maps package
kinds to `required` and `excluded` top-level fields. The published policy excludes `private` entirely;
`"private": false` is also forbidden so publishability has one canonical representation.

```jsonc
// ✅ Central, editable policy.
"packageJson": {
  "published": {
    "required": ["name", "version", "description", "license", "repository"],
    "excluded": ["private"]
  },
  "dev": {
    "required": [],
    "excluded": []
  }
}

// ❌ A published payload is missing required metadata or carries the forbidden field.
{ "name": "@scope/library", "version": "1.0.0", "private": false }
```

## NR-10: Declare runtime compatibility `[GAP]`

> Every inventory entry declares runtime compatibility.

Old number: 2.1.9.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check package-json`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: module-kind.ts ignores file extensions: package.json {"type":"module","main":"./index.cjs"} with manifest type esm, or {"type":"commonjs","exports":{".":"./index.mjs"}} with manifest type cjs, both pass (verified by calling consumerModuleKinds) although the entry point is the other format. Fix: issue I-76.

Issues: I-76.

Every manifest entry also declares two capabilities independent of `kind`: `type` is `cjs`, `esm` or `dual`, and
`browser` states whether browser execution is supported. `kind` describes ownership and publication; these fields
describe runtime compatibility.

`type` is `cjs`, `esm` or `dual` and must agree with
the real `package.json` type and entry points; `browser` is an explicit boolean capability claim, never an omission.

```jsonc
// ✅ A Node-only package with both CommonJS and ESM entry points.
{ "kind": "published", "type": "dual", "browser": false }

// ✅ A browser-capable ESM package.
{ "kind": "published", "type": "esm", "browser": true }
```

## NR-14: Match the tsc mode to the tsconfig shape `[GAP]`

> A `tsc` invocation matches its tsconfig's shape.

Old number: 2.1.13.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check tsc-mode`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Three changes pass. (1) Bare tsc with a valued flag: "lint": "tsc --noEmit --pretty false" on a solution-style ./tsconfig.json; the positional `false` makes the parser skip the invocation (tsc-mode.ts:121). (2) Inheritance: "lint": "tsc -p ./tsconfig.lint.json --noEmit" where tsconfig.lint.json is `{ "extends": "./tsconfig.json", "references": [...] }` and ./tsconfig.json has "files": []; isSolutionStyle reads the raw file, sees no `files`, and passes, while tsc inherits the empty `files` and checks nothing. (3) A path-qualified binary, `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p ...`: the token is not `tsc` (tsc-mode.ts:98). Only package.json scripts of inventoried packages are read; a tsc call in the Makefile, a shell script or fhevm-npm/package.json is not. Fix: issue I-77.

Issues: I-77.

A solution-style tsconfig (empty `files` plus
`references`) must be driven with `tsc -b`: project mode (`tsc -p`, or bare `tsc`) loads it, checks zero files and
exits 0 — the silent failure TS18002 would catch, except `references` suppresses it. Leaves may use either mode.

```jsonc
// ✅ Build mode walks the references of the solution file.
"lint": "tsc -b ./tsconfig.json --noEmit"

// ❌ Project mode on { "files": [], "references": [...] } checks nothing and still passes.
"lint": "tsc -p ./tsconfig.json --noEmit"
```

## NR-15: Link a member by directory, not by version `[GAP]`

> A member depending on another member uses a relative `file:` link to that member's directory.

Old number: 3.1.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check dependencies`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: An npm alias: in hardhat/v3/plugin/package.json add "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext-prev1": "npm:@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext@^0.13.0". The declared name is the alias, so `members.has(declaration.name)` is false (dependencies.ts:183) and npm fetches the registry copy of a member by version. The repository already uses this alias pattern for @fhevm/sdk-prev1. Fix: issue I-78.

Issues: I-01, I-78.

This
applies to intra-workspace dependencies only — a member naming another manifest member, such as a plugin depending on
`@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext`. External packages (`eslint`, `hardhat`, `@fhevm/sdk`) are untouched and follow
[NR-28](../entries/NR-28.md) to [NR-39](../entries/NR-39.md). npm installs the link as a symlink, whatever installation root each side lives in, so bumping the target's
version changes no dependency spec and no lockfile edge. A version pin would do the opposite: the moment the member's
version moves past the pin, npm silently fetches npmjs.com's package of that name instead of linking the member.

An npm-distributed package may link only an npm-published member: the publish layer renders the link to a registry
range, and there is nothing to render a private helper to. The link is legal in the working tree precisely because
publication rewrites it; an unrendered `file:` spec must never reach npmjs.com.

```jsonc
// ✅ In hardhat/v2/e2e: a symlink to hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg, and still one after the plugin bumps.
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:../plugin/pkg"

// ✅ In hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg (npm-distributed) to an npm-published member of another root.
//    Rendered to a registry range at publish time.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "file:../../../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg"

// ❌ Names the member by version. Correct today; after the plugin bumps to 0.4.3 npm fetches
//    npmjs.com's 0.4.2, and the workspace stops testing the member without a word.
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "0.4.2"

// ❌ A range has the same failure, one step earlier.
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "^0.5.0"

// ❌ A link must resolve to the manifest member having this package name.
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:../../another-package/pkg"

// ❌ An npm-distributed package linking a private helper: a published tarball cannot resolve it,
//    and nothing can render it.
"@fhevm/sdk-common-dev": "file:../../../common"
```

## NR-16: No tarball spec for a member `[GAP]`

> Never use `file:*.tgz` for a name that is also a member.

Old number: 3.1.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check dependencies`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: A non-member source inside the workspace: add "devDependencies": { "@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:../../tarballs/fhevm-hardhat-plugin-0.4.2.tgz" } to hardhat/v2/package.json (kind workspace-root, member=false). No check reads a cluster root's dependency specs except the forbidden and pinned lists, yet npm resolves that root with its members, which is the failure the rule describes. Fix: issue I-79.

Issues: I-79.

npm links members by name before reading the spec,
so the tarball is ignored and the edge is marked `invalid` — after which the whole subtree stops resolving.

```jsonc
// ✅ Same package, linked as a directory instead of packed. No pack step, nothing to rebuild first.
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:../plugin/pkg"

// ❌ In hardhat/v2/e2e, while @fhevm/hardhat-plugin is a member at hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg. npm reports:
//    invalid: "file:...fhevm-hardhat-plugin-0.4.2.tgz" from hardhat/v2/e2e -> ./hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg
//    ...and then leaves this member's other dependencies unresolved, while `npm install` says "up to date".
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:../../../tarballs/fhevm-hardhat-plugin-0.4.2.tgz"
```

## NR-18: Declare every package you use `[VIOLATED]`

> Declare every package whose API or executable you use.

Old number: 3.3.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check dependencies`

Evidence:

- `hardhat/v3/plugin/test/deploy.test.ts:8` shows an import of `@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext/ts` on `release/0.14.x`, which `hardhat/v3/plugin/package.json` does not declare, and `fhevm-npm/base/checks/dependencies.ts:31-50` compares source imports only with root pins. Fix: issue I-53, pushed on a branch, not yet merged.

Issues: I-01, I-53.

This includes packages imported by
source files and tools invoked by npm scripts; script-only tools belong in `devDependencies`. A package resolved only
through hoisting is a phantom dependency: it disappears under a different install strategy, and non-node tools never
find it at all.

```jsonc
// ✅ hardhat/v2/e2e imports chai and hardhat-ethers in its tests, so it declares both.
"devDependencies": { "@nomicfoundation/hardhat-ethers": "^3.1.3", "chai": "^4.5.0", "hardhat": "^2.29.1" }

// ❌ The same imports, undeclared. They resolve only because another member's copies sit hoisted in the
//    installation root's node_modules.
"devDependencies": { "hardhat": "^2.29.1" }

// ✅ A script invokes eslint, and the package declares the tool itself.
{ "scripts": { "lint": "eslint" }, "devDependencies": { "eslint": "^10.13.0" } }

// ❌ eslint happens to be hoisted from the workspace root but is undeclared here.
{ "scripts": { "lint": "eslint" } }
```

> On `release/0.14.x`, `hardhat/v3/plugin/test/deploy.test.ts:8` imports `@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext/ts`, which
> `hardhat/v3/plugin/package.json` does not declare; `fhevm-npm/base/checks/dependencies.ts:31-50` compares source
> imports only with root pins. Fix: issue I-53, pushed on a branch, not yet merged.

## NR-19: Tell tools that do not walk up where to look `[GAP]`

> Tools that do not walk up must be told where to look.

Old number: 3.3.2.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: In hardhat/v3/e2e/foundry.toml change libs to `["dependencies", "node_modules"]`. Every `fhevm-npm check` passes. `forge build` fails later only if a contract imports a hoisted package. Fix: issue I-81.

Issues: I-01, I-81.

`forge` searches only the directories in `libs`, so a
hoisted `@openzeppelin` is invisible to it unless the installation root's `node_modules` is listed explicitly.

```toml
# ✅ The installation root's node_modules is listed, so forge finds what npm hoisted there.
libs = ["dependencies", "node_modules", "../../node_modules"]

# ❌ Only this package's own node_modules. A hoisted @openzeppelin is invisible, and forge reports
#    "Source ... not found" naming only this directory — which looks like a missing install.
libs = ["dependencies", "node_modules"]
```

## NR-20: Forbidden packages need an exact exception `[GAP]`

> Globally forbidden packages appear in no dependency section unless the exact package has an exception.

Old number: 3.3.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check dependencies`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: The check compares the declared name only. In hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg/package.json add "sh": "npm:solhint@^5.0.0": the name 'sh' is not forbidden, and `check lint-policy` skips mirror-only trees (lint-policy.ts:24, :94-107). For any forbidden name other than solhint the alias passes in every package, because the lint-policy scan hard-codes 'solhint' (lint-policy.ts:8). Fix: issue I-82.

Issues: I-82.

The
manifest lists forbidden names in `dependencies.forbidden`; a `dependencyExceptions` entry permits only that one
package, never siblings or children. An exception naming no declared dependency is stale and fails validation.

```jsonc
// ✅ One narrowly scoped exception.
{
  "dependencies": { "forbidden": ["legacy-linter"] },
  "packages": {
    "./standalone-template": { "dependencyExceptions": ["legacy-linter"] }
  }
}

// ❌ No package-specific exception permits this declaration.
"devDependencies": { "legacy-linter": "^1.0.0" }
```

<a id="nr-21"></a>

## NR-21: One spec for each pinned dependency `[GAP]`

> A pinned external dependency is declared with the same spec everywhere.

Old number: 3.3.4.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check pinned-dependencies`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Add @fhevm/sdk-prev1 with its exact pinned npm alias spec to a nongeneration helper such as common/package.json, or retain it on the previous generation during an approved rotation. The pin check compares the text but has no role-alias ownership test; it does not require the declaring package to be <vN>. Fix: issue I-83.

Issues: I-01, I-09, I-83.

`npm-manifest.json` maps a package
name to one spec in `dependencies.pinned`; every inventoried package that declares that name, in any dependency
section, repeats that spec verbatim. This exists for a dependency the workspace consumes but does not build:
`versions.json` is keyed by manifest package key, so it cannot name a payload outside the inventory, and a root pin in
the workspace root's `package.json` reaches only the private kinds that rule [NR-31](../entries/NR-31.md) covers. Without a single declared spec, two
installation roots silently resolve different copies of the same package. The comparison is textual, not semantic —
`1.2.2` and `^1.2.2` install the same version today but diverge on the next patch release, so the pin fixes the
range operator too. A pin no inventoried package declares is stale and fails validation.

Each installation root's `package-lock.json` copies these specs out of the manifests it locks, so aligning a
`package.json` without regenerating the lock leaves that copy behind and `npm ci` refuses the mismatch. The lockfile
copies are therefore checked against the pin too, `node_modules` entries excluded — those are resolved output rather
than a declared spec. Regenerate an installation root with `npm install --package-lock-only`, and an isolated consumer
fixture with `fhevm-npm test-consumer-regenerate-package-lock`.

The pin also names the version the workspace develops and releases against: `^1.2.2` says 1.2.2. A range is
resolved when a lockfile is written, so a root locked after a newer release silently takes it instead; the pin then
misstates what is installed, and roots locked at different times resolve different copies. Every copy a lockfile
resolves for a pinned name is therefore checked too — top-level or nested under another dependency, in an
installation root or a consumer fixture, and an npm alias under its alias name — and each must be **exactly the
pinned version**. A newer copy means the pin is behind: `make sync-pinned` moves it up (its `sync pinned` step raises
the manifest pin to the newest version a lockfile resolves, and `sync pinned --check` fails until it has), so a
release always carries the most recent package. An older copy means a lockfile was left behind a moved pin: npm
keeps a locked version while it still satisfies the range, so delete its entry and let npm resolve it again (`npm
install --package-lock-only` in an installation root, `fhevm-npm test-consumer-regenerate-package-lock <fixture>` for
a consumer fixture; `npm update` fails with ERESOLVE in a workspace whose members declare the package as a peer).

```text
❌ ./package-lock.json: '@scope/pkg' resolves to 1.2.3 at 'node_modules/@scope/pkg', newer than its pin "^1.2.2":
   the pin is behind what is installed. Move it to "^1.2.3" in npm-manifest.json#dependencies.pinned
```

```jsonc
// ✅ One spec named once, repeated by every consumer whatever its kind or dependency section.
{
  "dependencies": { "pinned": { "@scope/pkg": "^1.2.2" } }
}
"devDependencies":  { "@scope/pkg": "^1.2.2" }  // a dev owner
"peerDependencies": { "@scope/pkg": "^1.2.2" }  // its published payload

// ❌ The same version, a different range operator. Diverges the moment 1.2.3 ships.
"devDependencies": { "@scope/pkg": "1.2.2" }

// ❌ A stale patch level no other package uses.
"devDependencies": { "@scope/pkg": "^1.2.1" }
```

A pin may be an npm alias, `npm:<name>@<version>`, so that one installation holds two versions of the same package
under two names, for instance a test that runs against two lines of a dependency. The alias is pinned under its own
name, with its full spec, and is compared like any other pin: the target is part of the spec. When the aliases name
roles rather than versions (`<name>` for the current line, `<name>-prev<k>` for k lines back), the specs move forward
together at each generation rotation, and only `<vN>` may declare them: `<vN-1>` drops them, so no name ever carries two
specs.

```jsonc
// ✅ The current line under its own name, the previous line under an alias.
{
  "dependencies": { "pinned": { "@scope/pkg": "^1.2.2", "@scope/pkg-prev1": "npm:@scope/pkg@^1.1.7" } }
}
"devDependencies": { "@scope/pkg": "^1.2.2", "@scope/pkg-prev1": "npm:@scope/pkg@^1.1.7" }

// ❌ The range without `npm:`: npm would fetch a registry package actually named @scope/pkg-prev1.
"devDependencies": { "@scope/pkg-prev1": "^1.1.7" }
```

<a id="nr-22"></a>

## NR-22: Depend on the current generation `[GAP]`

> A dependency on a generation family targets `<vN>`; the only edge into `<vN-1>` is `<vN>`'s upgrade-test devDependency on the `<vN-1>` dev package.

Old number: 3.4.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check generations`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: an npm alias hides the target name: in ./hardhat/v3/e2e add "dependencies": {"hcc-prev": "npm:@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext@0.13.6"}; no family package is named hcc-prev, so no edge is resolved (verified with validateGenerationDependencies), and check dependencies 3.1.1 also keys on the alias name. Fix: issue I-84.

Issues: I-84.

Any package of the family (the dev package, its payload, its consumers)
counts as that generation. A `file:` spec is resolved by directory; a version spec by name, and when the name is
shared by several generations the spec must be the exact version of one of them, otherwise the validator cannot tell
which generation is meant. A generation may always depend on itself. The one cross-generation edge is narrow on all
three axes: the source is the `<vN>` dev package itself (not its payload, not a consumer below it), the target is the
`<vN-1>` **dev** package (not its payload), and the field is `devDependencies` (`<vN-1>` exists only to be tested
against, so nothing may put it on a shipping path). Every other edge into the family — a consumer on `<vN-1>`, anyone
on a generation that is neither — fails. The rule also covers a dependency no committed `package.json` declares: the
spec the Hardhat template mirror patch injects into the rendered template is resolved as if the template package had
declared it.

```jsonc
// ✅ In hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg: the current generation's payload.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "file:../../../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg"

// ✅ In host-contracts-cleartext/<vN> (<vN>): the <vN-1> dev package, for the upgrade e2e. The only edge into <vN-1>.
"devDependencies": { "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext-<vN-1>-dev": "file:../<vN-1>" }

// ❌ In host-contracts-cleartext/<vN> (<vN>): the same target from a runtime field. <vN-1> is for tests only.
"dependencies": { "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext-<vN-1>-dev": "file:../<vN-1>" }

// ❌ In host-contracts-cleartext/<vN> (<vN>): <vN-1>'s payload rather than its dev package.
"devDependencies": { "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "file:../<vN-1>/pkg" }

// ❌ In host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg: below <vN> is not <vN>; only the dev package carries the edge.
"devDependencies": { "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext-<vN-1>-dev": "file:../../<vN-1>" }

// ❌ In hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg: a consumer on <vN-1>. When <vN+1> arrives this is the pin that is forgotten.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "file:../../../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg"

// ❌ In common: nothing outside <vN> may depend on <vN-1>.
"devDependencies": { "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext-<vN-1>-dev": "0.0.0" }

// ❌ A range over a name two generations share: which payload is meant cannot be read off the spec.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "^<N>.0"
```

## NR-23: Vendored copies cover exactly the live generations `[HOLD]`

> Every vendored destination under a generation family sits in a live generation, and every live generation is among the directories that receive a face.

Old number: 3.4.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check generations`

A copy of `common-vendored/src` is declared on its destination package's
`vendored` entry in `npm-manifest.json` ([NR-42b](../entries/NR-42b.md)), and nowhere else. The check reads the destinations back out of those
entries: the entries with a local `source` that carry the same `files` under the same `rewrites` and `renamed` form one
destination; an entry pinned to an upstream origin is no part of one. A destination's `to` lists every directory that
receives its files. That grouping is what lets the check ask whether every live generation is among them. Each path
below the family directory must be under `<vN>` or `<vN-1>`. A path left under a retired generation is the entry a rotation
forgets, and it makes `fhevm-npm sync vendored` write into a generation nothing depends on. The converse half matters
more: a live generation missing from a destination, because its payload carries no such entry, receives no copy and no
byte comparison, so its committed copy drifts from `common-vendored/src` unnoticed — the exact failure that file exists
to prevent. One destination writes one face, so its entries must sit at the same path below their generation directory;
that is what lets a missing generation be named as the entry to add. A destination whose family paths are all retired is
reported only as something to retarget.

The one exception is a face NAMED for a generation, `<name>-<gen>.<ext>` by its SOURCE name — for
example `cleartext-config-<vN>.ts`, the complete TypeScript face rule [NR-42c](../entries/NR-42c.md)'s generator emits for <vN>, which lands in <vN>'s
pkg/ts `renamed` to the stable `cleartext-config.ts`. It exists for one generation by construction, so it is not
demanded of the others; what is demanded is the converse, that it lands in the generation it is named for and nowhere
else, and that it travels in an entry of its own. <vN>'s face copied into <vN-1> would hand <vN-1> constants its contracts
have no field for.

```jsonc
// Entries of npm-manifest.json#packages, their other fields left out.
// ✅ One face, the same entry on both live generations' payloads.
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg":   { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts/types", "files": ["shared.ts"], "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg": { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts/types", "files": ["shared.ts"], "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }

// ✅ <vN>'s face lands in <vN> alone, in its own entry, under the stable name.
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg": { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts", "files": ["cleartext-config.ts"], "renamed": { "cleartext-config.ts": "cleartext-config-<vN>.ts" }, "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }

// ❌ <vN>'s face copied into <vN-1> too: values <vN-1>'s contracts have no field for.
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg": { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts", "files": ["cleartext-config.ts"], "renamed": { "cleartext-config.ts": "cleartext-config-<vN>.ts" }, "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }

// ❌ After the pair rotates to <vN+1>/<vN>: only <vN>'s payload carries the entry. <vN+1>, the new current generation, is missing, so it silently keeps a stale copy.
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN+1>/pkg": { /* no entry for shared.ts */ }
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg":   { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts/types", "files": ["shared.ts"], "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }

// ❌ <vN-2> is retired: the entry sits on a generation `generations` no longer lists.
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-2>/pkg": { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts/types", "files": ["shared.ts"], "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }

// ❌ One set of files, two faces: which face is a missing generation owed?
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg":   { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts", "files": ["x.ts"], "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg": { "vendored": [{ "relPath": "./ts/types", "files": ["x.ts"], "source": "./common-vendored/src", "reason": "…" }] }
```

## NR-24: The cleartext config names the live generations `[HOLD]`

> `cleartext-config.json#appliesTo.generations` names exactly the live generations.

Old number: 3.4.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check generations`

The generator writes a
face into `host-contracts-cleartext/<gen>/` for every listed key, so the list must equal `<vN>` and `<vN-1>` by directory
basename. A retired key makes the generator write into a directory that no longer exists; a live generation missing
from the list receives no face, and `fhevm-npm check cleartext-config` cannot miss a face it was never told to expect.

```jsonc
// ✅ With generations.current = ./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN> and previous = ./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>
"appliesTo": { "generations": ["<vN-1>", "<vN>"] }

// ❌ <vN-2> is retired, and <vN> — live — would get no face.
"appliesTo": { "generations": ["<vN-2>", "<vN-1>"] }
```

## NR-25: Only the current payload is a member `[HOLD]`

> `<vN>`'s published payload is a workspace member; `<vN-1>`'s is not.

Old number: 3.4.4.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check generations`

Issues: I-01, I-08.

Both generations publish one npm name, so
at most one of their payloads may be listed in an installation root — and it must be the one every consumer resolves.
A generation's payload is the directory its dev package names in `publishedRelPath`. This is the flag a rotation
forgets: left behind, the retired payload keeps claiming the shared name, and rule [NR-04](../entries/NR-04.md) then reports a name assigned to
two members plus a member missing from its installation root's `workspaces` — two consequences, neither of which names the
field that is wrong.

```jsonc
// ✅ With generations.current = ./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN> and previous = ./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg": { "kind": "published", "member": true }
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg": { "kind": "published", "member": false }

// ❌ After the pair rotates to <vN+1>/<vN>: the retired payload still claims the shared published name.
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg": { "kind": "published", "member": true }
```

## NR-26: Only the current generation has upgrade scripts `[GAP]`

> `<vN>` declares the upgrade scripts, `test:upgrade` and any `test:upgrade:*`; `<vN-1>` declares none.

Old number: 3.4.5.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check generations`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/generations.ts:384-430` reads only the exact name `test:upgrade`, so a `test:upgrade:fast` left on <vN-1> passes. Fix: forbid every script whose name starts with `test:upgrade` on <vN-1>.

Issues: I-09, I-50.

A generation proves most of itself alone, but the upgrade FROM the older generation it can only prove against a real
`<vN-1>` stack. That suite therefore lives behind its own verbs, `test:upgrade` and its variants such as
`test:upgrade:fast`, and the Makefile asks them of `<vN>` only — so a rotation retires the older generation's upgrade
suite by moving the pair, with nothing to remember inside the package. Each verb holds its commands DIRECTLY rather
than chaining `npm run` leaves: the scripts to delete when the suite goes are exactly the `test:upgrade*` ones, and no
leaf is left behind to look like coverage. The rule holds both ends. Missing on `<vN>`: a generation was wired up
without the one suite that exercises the migration consumers will actually run. Any of them still present on `<vN-1>`:
the verb outlived the generation it upgraded from, so nothing invokes it, nothing fails, and it reads as coverage that
is not there. Every family has a `<vN-1>`, as [NR-87](../entries/NR-87.md) requires, so the rule applies to every family.

```jsonc
// ✅ In host-contracts-cleartext/<vN> (<vN>): the self-contained lane, then the cross-generation ones.
"test": "npm run test:forge && npm run test:templates:run && npm run test:harness:run && npm run test:create2-deploy-e2e"
"test:upgrade": "node internal/upgrade/cli/runUpgradeE2e.ts && node --test test/e2e/upgrade/create2.test.ts"
"test:upgrade:fast": "../../scripts/forge-test.sh --match-path 'test/upgrade/*' && …"

// ✅ In host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1> (<vN-1>): `test` only. Its own upgrade suite went with <vN-2>.
"test": "npm run test:forge && npm run test:templates:run && npm run test:harness:run"

// ❌ In <vN-1> after a rotation: a verb whose previous generation no longer exists.
"test:upgrade": "node internal/upgrade/cli/runUpgradeE2e.ts && node --test test/e2e/upgrade/create2.test.ts"

// ❌ In <vN-1> after a rotation: the fast variant, left behind because only `test:upgrade` was removed.
"test:upgrade:fast": "../../scripts/forge-test.sh --match-path 'test/upgrade/*' && …"

// ❌ In <vN>: one lane for everything. The upgrade suite then runs for <vN-1> too, against a stack that is gone.
"test": "npm run test:forge && node internal/upgrade/cli/runUpgradeE2e.ts"
```

## NR-27: The previous generation matches its release branch `[GAP]`

> `<vN-1>` is byte-identical to the release branch that owns it, minus whatever a rotation deleted.

Old number: 3.4.6.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check generation-parity`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: the check SKIPS (exit 0, note printed) when the release branch does not resolve, and nothing checks that CI fetches it: change fetch-depth: 0 to 1 in .github/workflows/sdk-cleartext-tests.yml and an in-place edit to host-contracts-cleartext/v13 passes CI. Fix: issue I-85.

Issues: I-13, I-85.

Global rule
[R-04](../../../global/rules/entries/R-04.md) states the same rule, and the two evolve separately. A generation is authored on its own release branch and then
keeps living here as `<vN-1>`, the stack `<vN>`'s upgrade suite upgrades FROM. That copy is not a fork: edit it in place and
the upgrade is rehearsed against a stack nobody ships, while the branch that does ship it says something else. The
branch is derived from the generation's own number — `<vN>` is owned by `release/<N>.x` — so nothing hardcodes a
version and a rotation needs no edit here. Resolution prefers the local branch and falls back to `origin/`.

A generation whose branch resolves neither way is SKIPPED, and the skip is printed at every verbosity and left out of
the "checked" count — a check that quietly did nothing must not read as one that passed. Skipping rather than failing
is what lets one file serve every branch: the release-branch practice began partway through, so v12 has no
`release/0.12.x` and never will, and `fhevm-npm` has to be identical on `release/0.13.x`, where v12 is `<vN-1>`, and on
`release/0.14.x`, where v13 is. The cost is that a branch which exists but was never fetched also skips, so CI must
fetch it to get real coverage.

The rule is DELIBERATELY one-directional. Files may exist on the release branch and not here: a rotation deletes
`<vN-1>`'s own upgrade lane ([NR-26](../entries/NR-26.md), and the generation's `ROTATION.md`), and those deletions are the point. What may
never happen is the other direction — a file here that differs from the branch, or that the branch never had. Both
mean the retired generation was edited in place instead of on the branch that owns it.

The generation's own `package.json` is the single exemption, and it is forced rather than chosen: [NR-26](../entries/NR-26.md) requires
`<vN-1>` to drop `test:upgrade` and [NR-22](../entries/NR-22.md) requires it to drop the dependency on the generation it upgraded from, yet
both lines are still present on the release branch, where that generation was `<vN>`. Exempting it leaves nothing
unguarded — those two rules own its content, and every nested `package.json` below it stays in scope.

```sh
# ✅ <vN-1> lost its six `upgrade` folders to the rotation and changed nothing else.
# ❌ host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/internal/constants.ts: differs from release/<N-1>.x
# ❌ host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/INVENTED.md: present in <vN-1> here but absent from release/<N-1>.x
```

`FHEVM_PARITY_REF_<GENERATION>` names a different ref to compare that generation against. It is for the window where
`<vN-1>` is brought across while the work it comes from is still on a topic branch, unmerged into the release branch
that owns it: until that merge lands the derived ref is the wrong baseline, and the honest alternative — turning the
check off — compares nothing at all. Two rules stop it becoming a mute button. An override is REPORTED on every run
that uses it, as a note rather than a verbose success, because a green run that never looked at the release branch has
not proved what this rule is about. And an override that does not resolve FAILS rather than skips: the skip above is
for a branch nobody created, whereas a ref someone typed is a ref they expect to exist.

```sh
FHEVM_PARITY_REF_V<N-1>=<topic branch> ./fhevm-npm-cli check generation-parity
# ⚠️  ./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>: compared with '<topic branch>' because
#     FHEVM_PARITY_REF_V<N-1> is set — this run does NOT prove parity with 'release/<N-1>.x'
```

## NR-28: The workspace root pins shared dependencies `[GAP]`

> The workspace root pins what the whole workspace shares.

Old number: 4.1.1.

Check: script.

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Two changes pass. (1) The rule's own bad example: delete "ethers" and "viem" from the `.` root's devDependencies; the 4.2.1 and 4.3.1 comparisons have nothing to compare with and stay silent. (2) A second place: add "devDependencies": { "ethers": "6.16.0" } to hardhat/v2/package.json; validatePrivateRootPins skips kind workspace-root (dependencies.ts:254-256), so a cluster root can declare a divergent spec. Fix: issue I-86.

Issues: I-01, I-86.

The `.` root's `package.json` is the one place a
shared spec is declared: the dependency checks compare packages with its specs alone, whichever installation root
installs them. Each installation root hoists its own copy: a member of the `.` root compiles against the `.` root's, and
a member of a cluster root such as `hardhat/v2` against its cluster's. For an exact pin, that copy is the pinned version
because the member repeats the root's spec ([NR-31](../entries/NR-31.md)); for a range, each installation root resolves its own version inside
the same range. These root-spec checks do not compare the resolved versions; a dependency pinned in
`npm-manifest.json#dependencies.pinned` still has every resolved copy held to its pin ([NR-21](../entries/NR-21.md)). Either way, a member
declaring something else publishes a claim nobody verified.

```jsonc
// ✅ In the workspace root's package.json. Exact, because these are the two whose ranges already diverged once.
"devDependencies": { "ethers": "6.17.0", "viem": "2.55.19" }

// ❌ No root pin, so every member states its own, and the installation roots lose their shared declaration
//    baseline: each resolves whatever its own members happen to declare.
"devDependencies": {}
```

## NR-30: Foundry projects inherit the format policy `[GAP]`

> Every Foundry project inherits the shared formatting policy.

Old number: 4.1.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check foundry`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Compliant change that fails: extends = { path = "../../foundry.base.toml", strategy = "replace-arrays" } in `[profile.default]`. Forge accepts the table form (the installed forge 1.5.1 binary contains the strategies `replace-arrays` and `no-collision`), but the regex at foundry.ts:204 accepts a quoted string only. Any other valid TOML spelling fails too, for example the header `[ profile.default ]`. NR-43c says a Foundry answer comes from `forge config --json`, never from a parsed foundry.toml; this is the one place that parses it. Also loose: only a foundry.toml in an inventoried package's own folder is read (foundry.ts:27-29), so a foundry.toml in a subfolder, without extends, passes. Fix: issue I-88.

Issues: I-01, I-49, I-88.

A package declaring a non-empty `forge:fmt`
script has a `foundry.toml` in the same directory. Every `foundry.toml` declares `[profile.default].extends` for
the workspace root's `foundry.base.toml`; `fhevm-npm check foundry` verifies that ownership and compares every project's effective `[fmt]`
values with the shared file. Package-specific `[fmt].ignore` values are exempt.

The one exception to `extends` is a `standalone` project: the consumer runner copies it out of the workspace and
installs it on its own, so where it runs there is no shared file to extend (forge treats a missing `extends`
target as a hard error). It restates the `[fmt]` policy inline instead, and `fhevm-npm check foundry` still compares its
effective values with the shared file — the exemption is from the mechanism, never from the policy.

```toml
# ✅ Package-local paths and compiler settings remain local; formatting policy is inherited.
[profile.default]
extends = "../../foundry.base.toml"

# ❌ No extends: future changes to the shared formatting policy would not reach this project.
[profile.default]
src = "pkg/src"
```

<a id="nr-31"></a>

## NR-31: Private packages repeat the root spec `[GAP]`

> A private workspace package declares every exact root pin it directly uses, and every private package repeats the root's spec for each root dependency it declares.

Old number: 4.2.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check dependencies`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: the 4.2.1 placement test in `fhevm-npm/base/checks/dependencies.ts` counts a script that runs an exact root pin's executable as a use, and asks a shared helper for `dependencies`; 3.3.1 asks for `devDependencies`. Fix: ignore script-only use in the 4.2.1 placement test, so `devDependencies` wins.

Issues: I-01, I-58.

The spec is repeated verbatim: an exact root pin exactly, a
ranged root spec with the same range. A different spec would claim support for a version the workspace did not test. Use
and placement are judged under this rule for an exact root pin only, on a `dev`, `shared-helper` or `internal-consumer`
package: a package whose own source files import the dependency, or whose npm scripts run one of its executables,
declares it, and a package that does neither does not declare it. Shared helpers use `dependencies` (importing them must
install their runtime requirements); dev owners and internal consumers use `devDependencies`, because neither ships as a
runtime package. A root dependency whose executable a script runs must be declared whatever the root's spec, in
`devDependencies`, under [NR-18](../entries/NR-18.md). For a shared helper whose script runs an exact root pin's executable, `devDependencies`
wins: a tool that only a script runs is not a runtime requirement of the helper. A private `standalone` fixture is held
to the verbatim match alone, for the root dependencies it declares.

```jsonc
// ✅ The workspace root's package.json is the version source of truth: one exact pin, one range.
"devDependencies": { "ethers": "6.17.0", "example-linter": "^3.1.0" }

// ✅ A private consumer imports ethers (4.2.1) and runs example-linter (3.3.1), so its manifest declares both,
//    each with the root's spec.
"devDependencies": { "ethers": "6.17.0", "example-linter": "^3.1.0" }

// ✅ common is a shared helper whose exported runtime imports viem.
"dependencies": { "viem": "2.55.19" }

// ❌ Missing: this package imports ethers but relies silently on the root's hoisted copy.
"devDependencies": {}

// ❌ A range is not the exact version the private package actually tests.
"devDependencies": { "ethers": "^6.17.0" }

// ❌ A different floor makes a claim the workspace does not verify.
"devDependencies": { "ethers": "^6.16.0" }

// ❌ Not the root's range: a ranged root spec is repeated verbatim too.
"devDependencies": { "example-linter": "^3.0.0" }

// ✅ Published payloads remain ranges whose floor matches the pin, as required by 4.3.1.
"peerDependencies": { "ethers": "^6.17.0" }
```

`fhevm-npm check dependencies` compares each private package's declarations with the root's specs and, for an exact root
pin, with what the package uses (the bare imports of its owned source files and the executables its npm scripts invoke),
keyed by the manifest inventory, and reports `4.2.1` on a missing, unused, misplaced or divergent declaration. Published
entries stay under [NR-35](../entries/NR-35.md); non-packages, and whatever a standalone project declares beyond the root's specs, under [NR-39](../entries/NR-39.md).

## NR-33: One range per dependency group `[GAP]`

> Packages a dependency group installs together declare identical ranges.

Old number: 4.2.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check dependencies`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/dependencies.ts:18` and `:398-401` compare only `dev`, `shared-helper` and `internal-consumer` packages; no check holds a standalone consumer's version inside the published payload's peer range. Fix: issue I-54.

Issues: I-09, I-54.

Within one
`dependencyGroup`, every `dev`, `shared-helper` and `internal-consumer` package declares the same range for a
dependency they share: they build against one hoisted copy, so a different range fails only the day a member is
installed alone. Members are compared with each other, not with a table, so a new group needs no edit. A [NR-15](../entries/NR-15.md)
`file:` link counts by the directory it resolves to, so siblings at different depths agree when they link the same
member. Two kinds in a group are bounded instead of compared: a published payload states the range its users may
have, and a standalone consumer, installed alone, may declare any version or range inside it.

```jsonc
// ✅ Installed together: hardhat/v3/plugin, hardhat/v3/e2e and the template agree.
"hardhat": "^3.20.0"

// ✅ The published hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg states what its users may have.
"peerDependencies": { "hardhat": "^3.0.0" }

// ✅ The standalone hardhat/v3/plugin/test-consumer/esm pins a version inside that peer range.
"hardhat": "3.15.0"

// ❌ hardhat/v3/e2e next to the plugin's ^3.20.0: one hoisted copy, two claims.
"hardhat": "^3.18.0"

// ❌ A standalone consumer outside the published peer range proves nothing a user can install.
"hardhat": "2.29.1"
```

## NR-37: Derived versions equal the central version `[GAP]`

Old number: 4.3.3.

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Delete the `version` field of the member's entry (for example `plugin/pkg` in hardhat/v3/package-lock.json): memberEntries() at version-check.ts:234 keeps only entries with `version !== undefined`, so the entry is skipped and `version check` passes; the `?? 'no version'` branch at :96 is unreachable. Low severity: npm writes the field itself. A missing root lockfile is also skipped (:207), but 6.1.1 reports that. Fix: issue I-92.

Issues: I-01, I-07, I-92.

A payload's `package.json` version; in every
installation root whose lockfile records the member — its own root, and any root that links it cross-root — the
`version` npm wrote for it; the version a committed generated file embeds, such as
`foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmVersion.sol`; and the version each isolated consumer
fixture's lockfile pins the payload at ([NR-66](../entries/NR-66.md)). The remedy is `fhevm-npm version apply`:
edit `versions.json`, preview with `--dry-run`, apply. It accepts a clean worktree or exactly one unstaged change, that
file; a central version only moves forward; `--allow-downgrade` waives that test whenever it is passed. It is meant for
an old version nothing was ever published under, which the flag does not check: `--check-npmjs` asks the registry only
whether the new version is already there. No dependency spec changes, because member edges are `file:` links ([NR-15](../entries/NR-15.md)).
When a generated file no longer embeds a version, or a consumer lockfile records none, `version apply` cannot rewrite
it, and the check names the generator or the lockfile regeneration to run instead. `npm version` is not a supported path
— it writes derived state first and `version check` fails on it.

```sh
# ✅ The whole workflow. `version apply` writes every derived place; none is edited by hand.
$EDITOR versions.json && make version-plan && make version-apply && git add -A . && git commit

# ❌ Writes package.json first, so the authority is now the one out of date.
npm --prefix hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg version patch
```

<a id="nr-38"></a>

## NR-38: Rendered ranges stop at the generation `[GAP]`

> A rendered dependency range is `~<version>`: the target's central version, up to the end of its generation.

Old number: 4.3.4.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli publish check`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Two installation roots contain same-named published payloads at 1.0.1 and 2.0.1. A plugin links the second directory and correctly renders ~2.0.1. validateRenderedRanges chooses the first same-named member and rejects it in favor of ~1.0.1. Reproduced; names are not globally unique. Fix: issue I-93.

Issues: I-01, I-93, I-123.

A generation is `major.minor` at every version, so a rendered range is a tilde on the target's central version. A
payload built against contracts `<N>.4` renders `~<N>.4`: at least the version it was built and tested against, up to
the next generation, which the tilde excludes. A tilde stops at the end of the generation both below 1.0
(`~0.14.4` stops before `0.15.0`) and from 1.0 on (`~1.0.4` stops before `1.1.0`). A caret does not: below 1.0 it
accepts the same versions as the tilde, but from 1.0 on `^1.0.4` accepts `1.1.0`, the next generation.

The floor is never lower than the version the payload was built against: a lower one lets a consumer who upgrades the
payload keep, from their lockfile, an older dependency that may lack a fix the payload relies on. A contracts patch
still never forces a payload release; the payload raises its floor on its next release. A prerelease central version
renders exactly, since a tilde range does not match prereleases. This is the one range policy; there is no per-edge
configuration.

The floor makes the publish order binding: `publish check --check-npmjs` requires a published version that satisfies
the range, so the target's version must be on npmjs.com before the payload that renders it.

```jsonc
// ✅ In the v3 plugin's tarball, rendered from the file: link by `publish pack` (target central <N>.4).
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "~<N>.4"

// ❌ A caret: from 1.0 on, ^<N>.4 accepts the next generation.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "^<N>.4"

// ❌ The generation floor: a consumer upgrading the plugin can keep contracts <N>.0-<N>.3 and miss a fix.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "~<N>.0"

// ❌ Exact: every contracts patch would force a plugin release, or leave consumers with two copies.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "<N>.4"
```

> **Changed.** Until issue I-123, the renderer wrote a caret below 1.0 and a tilde from 1.0 on. Below 1.0 both accept the same versions, so no published range changes its meaning.

## NR-42: Content-integrity checks have conventional names `[HOLD]`

> Content-integrity capabilities have conventional check entry points.

Old number: 5.1.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

A manifest entry declaring `vendored`
requires `check:vendored-origin`; one declaring `mirror` conventionally exposes `check:mirror`, OPTIONAL until the
mirror spec is implemented — requiring an unpassable script would be enforcement theater. The owner is the dev
package for a published entry (inverse of `publishedRelPath`), otherwise the entry itself; implementations are
package-owned, and CI invokes the conventions.

`mirror.repository` identifies an independent Git repository that must stay synchronized with the local entry.
Mirroring is a capability, not a kind; `check:mirror` owns the package-specific contract.

A vendored SOURCE may itself be generated: each generation's `common-vendored/src/cleartext-config-<vN>.ts` is rendered
from `cleartext-config.json` by `fhevm-npm generate cleartext-config` (common-vendored's `generate` script), then
`sync vendored` fans the committed result out — regenerate before syncing; `make generate` runs both in order. The same
command also writes each generation's `pkg/src/cleartext/shared/LibFhevmCleartextConfig.sol` and
`scripts/cleartext-config.sh` directly — no sync hop, because nothing imports those files across packages.

```jsonc
// ✅ The manifest describes the copies without prescribing how they are checked.
"vendored": [
  {
    "relPath": "./src/internal/vendored",
    "source": "./common-vendored/src",
    "reason": "The published package cannot import a private workspace helper."
  }
]

// ✅ Mirroring is orthogonal to kind and records only the independent repository.
"mirror": { "repository": "https://github.com/example/project" }

// ✅ In the owner's real package.json. Each conventional command owns its implementation.
"scripts": {
  "check:vendored-origin": "node ./internal/check-vendored-origin.ts",
  "check:mirror": "node ./internal/check-mirror.ts"
}

// ❌ Per-element command paths couple inventory data to one check implementation.
"checkedBy": "./scripts/check-vendored-origin.ts"

// ❌ A declared capability exists, but CI has no conventional command to discover.
"scripts": {}
```

<a id="nr-42a"></a>

## NR-42a: A pinned vendored copy records a digest `[HOLD]`

> A pinned vendored copy records a content digest, and every build verifies it.

Old number: 5.1.3a.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli sync vendored --check`

Issues: I-21.

A pinned `source` names an
upstream repository and commit; `source.digest` records what the copies hash to once written. `sync vendored --check`
recomputes it from the files on disk and fails on any difference, so a build proves the copies are untouched without
git, a network call, or the upstream repository being present anywhere. That last point is the reason the digest exists:
reading the commit itself only ever worked in the upstream repository, because the workspace then vendored from the
repository it lived in. Copied out — which is how a mocks workspace is made — every pinned entry failed.

The digest is never typed by hand, and `sync vendored` never writes it: a value that gates every build belongs in a
diff somebody read, and the sync's job is to make the copies match the manifest, not the other way round.
`sync vendored --digest` downloads each pinned tree and prints the digest it implies; `--check` prints the one the
local copies produce. THE ONE WRITER is `bump vendored <package> --tag <tag>`: it moves every pin under that package
key (a generation and its nested `pkg`) to the tag — commit resolved from the tag, digest computed from upstream,
copies rewritten, each owning `package.json#fhevm.vendoredFrom` regenerated — as ONE change, which is the diff to
read. Scoped by package on purpose, and all of a package's pins together: a generation's contracts and config must
sit at one commit (two pins from one upstream at two commits is the drift a hand edit produces), while two
GENERATIONS pin that same upstream at deliberately different tags, so "every pin from this repository" would be wrong.

Two consequences worth knowing. The digest proves the copies match what was RECORDED, not what upstream holds — the
provenance check is `sync vendored` itself, which fetches the pinned trees, from upstream or from its cache, unless run
with `--check`, so a release should run it and fail if it rewrites anything. And because the copies are formatted before
hashing, the digest is tied to `foundry.version`: a forge release that changes `forge fmt` invalidates every digest at
once, and the failure reads as tampering unless you know to re-run the sync after a toolchain bump.

```jsonc
// ✅ The pin says where the copies came from; the digest says what they are.
"source": {
  "repository": "https://github.com/zama-ai/fhevm",
  "tag": "v0.12.5",
  "commit": "ac18e49ea85dd3c26788fc66f9ac0ea7cfe48519",
  "from": "host-contracts/contracts",
  "digest": "sha256-AAWuLw11xwMmEiFB0skWiKwIhOOYf6bDaP3ssnp/pzA="
}

// ❌ A pin with no digest. The copies are unverified, and the check says so rather than passing quietly.
"source": { "repository": "…", "tag": "v0.12.5", "commit": "ac18e49…", "from": "host-contracts/contracts" }
```

<a id="nr-42b"></a>

## NR-42b: Declare vendored copies only in the manifest `[VIOLATED]`

> `npm-manifest.json` is the only place a vendored copy is declared.

Old number: 5.1.3b.

Check: script.

Evidence:

- `fhevm-npm/base/checks/inventory.ts:128-130` shows a vendored `source` resolved from the git root, while `fhevm-npm/base/sync-vendored.ts:64` resolves it from the workspace root. Fix: issue I-55.

Issues: I-01, I-21, I-55.

What is copied, where it lands, which
files, and what is rewritten on arrival all live on the destination package's `vendored` entry. Nothing else declares
a copy, and no second file restates one.

This was two files once: `common-vendored/manifest.json` said which files went where, and the manifest restated the
same destinations and file lists per package. Two files describing one thing can only agree by luck, and eventually
did not — each side was resolved against a different base, so moving the workspace out of `<repo>/sdk/` failed a
comparison that was never about the bytes. The manifest wins because it already owns what a package CONTAINS: the
schema refuses `vendored` on a non-package or a workspace root, and the lint-policy, script and inventory checks
already read it there.

A `rewrite` belongs to the destination for the same reason. It exists because THIS package resolves an import
differently from the package the bytes came from — a fact about the consumer, not about the source.

So does a `renamed` entry, destination name to source name, for a copy that changes name on arrival. It exists for one
case: each generation's `pkg/ts/cleartext-config.ts` is common-vendored's `cleartext-config-<gen>.ts`, so the module a
consumer imports keeps one stable name while the generation lives in the source file's name — and in nothing a
consumer writes. Keyed by the destination so `files` keeps meaning "what sits in relPath"; every key must be listed
there, and only a local copy can be renamed.

The copy map `sync vendored` walks is derived from the manifest, grouping entries by the file set they carry, so
"these generations receive an identical copy" is still one destination with several `to` paths and rule [NR-23](../entries/NR-23.md) can
still ask whether every live generation is among them.

```jsonc
// ✅ One entry says everything: the source, the files, and the edit this package needs on arrival.
"vendored": [{
  "relPath": "./src/internal/vendored",
  "files": ["ethersEthereumLib.ts", "fhevm-chains.ts"],
  "source": "./common-vendored/src",
  "rewrites": [{ "file": "ethersEthereumLib.ts", "from": "from './ethereumLibTypes.ts';", "to": "from '@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext/ts';" }],
  "reason": "A published package cannot depend on a private workspace member."
}]

// ❌ A second manifest repeating the destination and its files. It can only ever drift from this one.
```

Every manifest path resolves against the workspace root ([NR-73a](../entries/NR-73a.md)).

<a id="nr-42c"></a>

## NR-42c: One upstream commit per generation `[GAP]`

> A generation pins ONE upstream commit, and every copy taken from upstream rides it.

Old number: 5.1.3c.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/vendored.ts:362-397` checks each pinned entry alone; no check compares the tag and commit of a generation's entries. Only `fhevm-npm/base/bump-vendored.ts:8-10` keeps them together. Fix: add the comparison.

Issues: I-09, I-21, I-61.

A generation's
published package pins `host-contracts/contracts` at a tag and commit; anything else the generation copies from the
same upstream — today `library-solidity/config`, which its dev package vendors into `internal/zama-config/` so
`check:zama-config` reads the localhost address set at the commit the contracts came from — names the SAME tag and
commit. Two entries, one pin: the second is the existing pin covering one more directory of the same tree, not a
second version to keep in step by hand.

The copy sits on the dev package, not the published one, because only `pkg/` ships and a file that exists to grade
a workspace constant must never reach a consumer. `package.json#fhevm.vendoredFrom` is singular, so a package can
carry one pinned entry — which is also why the config cannot join `pkg`'s entry and lives on the dev owner. A
retired generation takes its copy with it (see each generation's `ROTATION.md`).

The same one-commit thinking governs `cleartext-config.json`'s `generations` field: a constant only one generation's
contracts have a field for is scoped to it, and the generator renders every face COMPLETE for its generation — one
`cleartext-config-<gen>.ts` per generation in common-vendored/src, each generation's Solidity and shell faces — so a
shared constant appears in each generation's faces as generated duplication from one JSON, never as a forked copy.

Reading the file from `@fhevm/solidity` in `node_modules` instead is wrong even though it is the same file: the
installed version is whatever the Hardhat packages pin, not the version line either generation vendors, so a green
check there would be a check against a config nothing in the generation builds.

```jsonc
// ✅ The dev package's entry repeats its pkg's tag and commit exactly. Rotating one means rotating both.
"./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>": {
  "kind": "dev",
  "vendored": [{
    "relPath": "./internal/zama-config",
    "source": { "repository": "https://github.com/zama-ai/fhevm", "tag": "<vN>.1", "commit": "e7e7fec…", "from": "library-solidity/config", "digest": "sha256-…" },

},

}
```

## NR-43b: Generators expose the full round trip `[GAP]`

> A package that generates exposes the full round trip.

Old number: 5.1.4b.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Wrong: verified, `clean:generate:exports` = `rm -rf pkg/ts ...` deletes the export-manifest output ./pkg/ts/index.ts yet fails 5.1.4b, since cleanRemoves (:499-501) wants the literal file path, not a parent directory or glob. Loose as well: a generator output not listed in export.manifest.json (e.g. pkg/templates written by generate:templates) can be dropped from clean:generated and nothing fails. Fix: issue I-97.

Issues: I-21, I-97.

Any package with `generate:*` scripts also defines a
non-empty `generate` aggregate and a non-empty `clean:generated` deleting every file the generators write; the
reverse holds too — `generate` or `clean:generated` with no `generate:*` leaf is dead wiring and is rejected.

Wiring is checked by name: every `generate:*` leaf must be reachable from `generate` through same-package `npm run`
references (exempt: `generate:genesis`, a stateful anvil deploy, and `generate:patch-sites`, a committed baseline a
test compares against), and every `export.manifest.json` output must be deleted by `clean:generated`.

This exists because a regenerate-and-diff gate cannot see a generator that silently _stops_ emitting a file: the
committed copy sits untouched, so nothing looks dirty. Deleting first turns that into a visible deletion, and the
delete list lives beside the generators — the only place it stands a chance of being kept current.

```jsonc
// ✅ Every path the generate:* scripts write is removable, and one verb rewrites everything.
// (Here the export manifest names only pkg/ts/index.ts.)
"scripts": {
  "clean:generated": "rm -rf pkg/abi pkg/templates pkg/ts/index.ts",
  "generate": "npm run generate:exports && npm run generate:templates",
  "generate:exports": "node ../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts generate exports ./export.manifest.json",
  "generate:templates": "node ./internal/cli/generateTemplates.ts"
}
```

```jsonc
// ❌ Generators with no way to prove they still emit everything.
"scripts": { "generate:exports": "node ../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts generate exports ./export.manifest.json" }
```

## NR-43c: A package can delete its build output `[GAP]`

Issues: I-21, I-43, I-98.

Every `dev`, `shared-helper` and
`internal-consumer` package that is not a mirror owner defines a non-empty `clean`. Its content requirements are
derived from what the package actually does, never listed centrally:

- a package whose scripts invoke `tsc` must delete `*.tsbuildinfo`, because a surviving build-info file lets the
  next typecheck resume from stale state;
- a Forge project must delete the directories `forge config --json` reports (`cache_path`, `out`, `broadcast`).

Those directory names are **asked of forge, never assumed** — `hardhat/v2/e2e` sets `cache_path = "cache-forge"`, so
any rule hard-coding `cache` is already wrong for some projects. Anywhere this repo needs a Foundry answer,
`forge config --json` (which resolves `extends`, profiles and defaults) is the source, never a parsed `foundry.toml`.

```jsonc
// ✅ Derived from what the package does: it runs tsc, and forge reports cache/out/broadcast.
"scripts": {
  "clean": "rm -rf cache out broadcast *.tsbuildinfo pkg/ts/_esm pkg/ts/_cjs",
  "compile:forge": "forge build --skip test"
}
```

```jsonc
// ❌ A rebuild resumes from stale incremental state.
"scripts": { "clean": "rm -rf out", "lint": "eslint && tsc -p ./tsconfig.json --noEmit" }
```

trees, so a Solhint configuration or directive there is not reported.

## NR-45: Use the workspace Prettier configuration `[GAP]`

> A non-published package running Prettier uses the workspace configuration, unless it is a template under a `…-dev` owner.

Old number: 5.1.6.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Compliant change that fails: a trailing comment on the statement line, `export { default } from '../prettier.base.mjs'; // shared base`. withoutComments removes only block comments and whole-line `//` comments, so the anchored regex no longer matches and the check reports `must contain: export { default } ...`. The rule says comments are ignored, in every package. Fix: issue I-100.

Issues: I-01, I-100.

It contains `prettier.config.js` re-exporting the workspace root's `prettier.base.mjs` by relative
path; the only accepted config filenames are those two. A dev owner containing only `package.json` and `pkg/` has no
local source to format, so any local Prettier config is forbidden. An installation root carries neither. Two packages
are spared the re-export. A mirror-only payload's dev owner need not carry it. A package at `<owner>/pkg` whose parent
`<owner>` is an inventoried package whose name ends in `-dev`, such as a workspace-native template, contains its own
`prettier.config.js` instead: users receive that template on its own, so `fhevm-npm check scripts` fails
a Prettier or ESLint config in it that imports, by a literal specifier, a workspace-only package or a relative or
absolute path that resolves lexically outside it. The check is static: it does not see a computed import or a URI
specifier such as `file:`, and it does not follow symlinks, so it is no proof that the config is self-contained at run
time.

**The workspace root is the sole exception: it holds both, and both are required.** `prettier.base.mjs` is the shared
base, and `prettier.config.js` re-exports it. The second is not a duplicate: `prettier.base.mjs` is not a filename
Prettier discovers, so the files that sit directly in the workspace root and belong to no package — `npm-manifest.json`,
`cleartext-config.json`, the root-level docs — are formatted with the shared base only through that re-export. Two
configs are allowed here; two sources of formatting truth are not, so the re-export is pinned to the one statement.

Comments are ignored when the statement is pinned, in every package: prose explaining a config is not a fork of it.

```js
// ✅ In an ESM common/prettier.config.js.
export { default } from '../prettier.base.mjs';

// ✅ In a CommonJS package's prettier.config.js.
module.exports = import('../../../prettier.base.mjs').then((module) => module.default);

// ✅ At the workspace root, beside prettier.base.mjs, comment and all.
export { default } from './prettier.base.mjs';

// ✅ In a template at <owner>/pkg under a `…-dev` owner: self-contained, nothing imported from the workspace.
export default { singleQuote: true, printWidth: 120 };
```

```text
❌ Alternate configuration filename:
.prettierrc.mjs

❌ At the workspace root, restating options instead of re-exporting the base:
export default { singleQuote: true };
```

## NR-46: Three ESLint layers `[GAP]`

> ESLint configuration has three layers: policy, layout, local.

Old number: 5.1.7.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: on `release/0.14.x`, `fhevm-npm/base/checks/scripts.ts:840-843` checks only the ESLint filenames inside packages; nothing checks the layout layer. Fix: the `validateEslintLayoutModules` check (issue I-62), pushed on a branch, not yet merged.

Issues: I-01, I-09, I-11, I-62.

- **Policy:** the workspace root holds the one `eslint.base.mjs`. It sets which rules apply and at what severity,
  and names no package path.
- **Entry:** every non-published package that defines `lint` contains `eslint.config.js`. It is the only file
  ESLint loads, and the only ESLint config filename allowed in a package. A dev owner that contains only
  `package.json` and `pkg/` has no ESLint config.
- **Layout:** which directories get which rules. A package states its layout in its own `eslint.config.js`. When
  two or more packages share the same layout, it may live once in a shared module, `<family>/eslint.<name>.mjs`.
  The module sits in the common parent folder of those packages, outside every package. It imports
  `eslint.base.mjs`, gives paths only, sets no rule, and is imported by each `eslint.config.js` that uses it, all
  of them below its folder. It is `.mjs` because the nearest `package.json` declares no `type`.
- **Local:** what belongs to one package only stays in its `eslint.config.js`: its own ignores, and a rule turned
  off for named files, with a comment that says why.

```text
✅ eslint.base.mjs                        policy
   <family>/eslint.<name>.mjs            layout shared by <family>/<vN>
   <family>/<vN>/eslint.config.js        entry + local
❌ <family>/<vN>/eslint.layout.mjs        a layout module inside a package
❌ <family>/eslint.<name>.mjs             imported by one package only: inline it
❌ eslint.config.mjs, .eslintrc.json      not the entry filename
```

<a id="nr-47"></a>

## NR-47: Dev owners define check:publint and check `[GAP]`

> Every dev owner of an npm-distributed payload defines `check:publint` and the `check` verb wrapping its deliverable validations.

Old number: 5.2.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `"check:publint": "publint ./pkg"` (the rule's own second ❌ example), `"check:publint": "echo ok"`, or dropping `&& attw --pack ./pkg` on a payload that ships types: `check scripts` passes. Fix: issue I-101.

Issues: I-101.

`check:publint` runs `publint --strict` against `pkg/`, and `attw --pack` against it too when
the payload ships type declarations; a Solidity-only payload ships none and runs `publint` alone. Every `check:*` leaf
must be reachable from `check`, except `check:mirror` (network-bound) and generator `--check` conveniences.

`attw --pack` resolves the packed types under node10, node16-cjs, node16-esm and bundler, and by default fails on a
problem in any of them. Under `--profile esm-only`, which an ESM-only payload passes, problems specific to node10 and
node16-cjs do not fail the gate; problems in node16-esm and bundler, and problems not tied to a resolution mode, still
can. Packing stays verified with no `.tgz`. The manifest gate follows `publishedRelPath` and requires these scripts, by
name, on the owning dev package; mirror-only payloads are exempt.

```jsonc
// ✅ --strict fails on warnings, and attw packs the package to resolve its types for real.
"check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg"

// ✅ An ESM-only payload: the same gate, under the profile that matches what it ships.
"check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg --profile esm-only"

// ✅ A Solidity-only payload: no types for attw to resolve.
"check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg"

// ❌ The required script entry is absent, so no uniform gate can discover the check.
"publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg"

// ❌ Warnings pass silently, and a payload that ships types never has them resolved, so a broken `exports` can ship.
"check:publint": "publint ./pkg"
```

installed declarations. For each installed published payload that declares a root entry point and types, `test-consumer`
therefore runs `tsc --traceResolution` on a one-line import of the package, fails if that import does not compile, and
proves two things: the trace names a declaration the installed `package.json` declares (`types`, `typings` or a `types`

and its opt-out value differs per major, so no generic check can pin it. The Hardhat v2 plugin's own test traces
`node10` instead (`hardhat/v2/plugin/test/node10-cjs-resolution.test.ts`, run by `make test-hh-v2-plugin`), against its
symlinked `pkg/` rather than an isolated installation.

```text
❌ /repo/hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg/src/index.ts
```
