## NR-52: Every payload file ships or is excluded `[GAP]`

> Every file in an npm-distributed payload directory is published or deliberately excluded.

Old number: 5.2.6.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check published-files`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Add a correctly whitelisted and packed src/café.ts. With Git's default core.quotePath, gitVisibleFiles returns a C-quoted escaped spelling, while npm returns the real UTF-8 path. The packed-set lookup reports the compliant file as stray. Newline/tab filenames similarly break the line-based reader. Fix: issue I-105.

Issues: I-105.

`files` is a
whitelist, so a file that sits beside it without being selected is dead weight: committed under `pkg/`, shipped to
nobody, reviewed by nobody. The check takes the repository-visible files of the payload directory (tracked and
untracked-unignored, as [NR-70](../entries/NR-70.md) discovers), asks npm what it would pack (`npm pack --dry-run`, scripts skipped), and
requires each file to be either in that tarball or matched by a `!` pattern in `files`. The `!` pattern is the one
place a deliberately unpublished file is declared; npm reads a pattern without a `/` at any depth, and so does the
check. A published package without `files` fails outright, since without the whitelist every stray file ships.
Mirror-only payloads are exempt: their directory is the mirror, and its unpublished files are the point.

```jsonc
// ✅ The tsconfig beside the sources is declared unpublished, so it may stay.
"files": ["src", "_types", "LICENSE", "README.md", "!**/tsconfig*.json", "!**/*.tsbuildinfo"]
```

```text
❌ pkg/NOTES.md      present, not selected by "files", named by no "!" pattern: delete it or declare it
❌ pkg/tsconfig.json present, "files": ["src", "_types"] says nothing about it
❌ no "files" at all in a published package.json
```

Evidence:

On a case-insensitive disk a file named `license` also passes there, but the Linux CI catches that one. Narrow: an npm-distributed payload is safe because npm does not pack a symlink and 5.2.6 then reports it. Fix: issue I-106.

Issues: I-07, I-106.

- Every published package sets `"license": "BSD-3-Clause-Clear"` exactly in its `package.json`, and a regular
  file named exactly `LICENSE` sits beside that `package.json`. The field supports registry metadata; the file
  ensures the payload carries the license text.

  `README.md` in `files`. They are the two files npmjs.com renders on a package page: the license text and the
  front page. npm packs both whatever `files` says, so the listing exists for the reader, not for npm: a whitelist

## NR-54: Wrapping dev packages define test:consumer `[GAP]`

> Every dev package that wraps an npm-distributed package defines `test:consumer`.

Old number: 5.3.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Add a Makefile target or workflow step running `npm --prefix host-contracts-cleartext/v14 run test:consumer:dev`: no check fails. Fix: issue I-107.

Issues: I-02, I-107.

This is the stable public
command for proving the installed payload; optional stages share the stem (`test:consumer:run`, …) but callers invoke
only `test:consumer`. A mirror-only consumer project is already the consumer and is exempt.

The published entry's `consumerTests` is the SOLE registry of its consumer tests: per module format the payload exposes
(CJS, ESM, both for a dual package — derived from the published entry points), a non-empty array of manifest package
keys. Nothing registers a consumer by existing: a `test-consumer/<format>` directory beside the payload, a `test`
script, or a `file:` dependency on the payload carry no registration semantics. A format may register several suites,
and one consumer may be registered by several payloads. `test-consumer` lists, selects and runs exactly the consumers
this registry names, and `test-consumer-regenerate-package-lock` regenerates their lockfiles.

```text
✅ dual package: "consumerTests": { "cjs": [...], "esm": [...] }
✅ ESM-only package: "consumerTests": { "esm": [...] }
❌ dual package registering only "esm"
❌ an existing test-consumer/cjs directory with no registration
```

```jsonc
// ✅ The v3 plugin exposes ESM and registers two ESM suites: its fixture and the Hardhat template.
{
  "type": "esm",
  "consumerTests": {
    "esm": ["./hardhat/v3/plugin/test-consumer/esm", "./hardhat/v3/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg"]
  }
}

// ❌ A boolean waiver would remove consumer coverage instead of locating it.
{ "consumerTests": false }

// ❌ The single-string spelling is retired; a registration is always an array.
{ "consumerTests": { "cjs": "./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg" } }
```

A registered consumer must execute as the selected module format, define a non-empty `test` script, and directly link
the tested package through a directory `file:` dependency. An isolated (non-member) consumer is a `standalone` fixture
and carries a committed `package-lock.json`; a workspace-member consumer is an `internal-consumer` or a mirror-only
`published` template and carries none ([NR-64](../entries/NR-64.md)). A consumer that is not itself a payload sets `private: true`. The
validator checks all of these; `test-consumer` performs the isolated installation and execution, replaying the
committed lockfile where one exists.

```jsonc
// ✅ In the dev package that wraps ./pkg. One command owns the whole consumer test.
"scripts": { "test:consumer": "node ../../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts test-consumer ./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg --run --build-linked-dependencies" }

// ❌ A package-specific name cannot be discovered or invoked uniformly.
"scripts": { "test:hardhat-template": "node ../../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts test-consumer ./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg --run --build-linked-dependencies" }
```

when they still reach the same node or account. Tests on an in-process chain, such as Hardhat's in-process network
or forge's per-test EVM, share nothing and need no serial mode. `test-consumer` itself runs consumer packages and
fixtures one at a time.

## NR-63: A tarball carries only registry specs `[GAP]`

> A tarball for an npm-distributed payload carries only registry specs and the central version.

Old number: 5.3.10.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli publish check`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: The same-named payloads in separate roots counterexample from NR-38 makes a correct ~2.0.1 tarball fail against the first member's ~1.0.1. Fix: issue I-112.

Issues: I-48, I-112.

`file:` links
are right in the tree ([NR-15](../entries/NR-15.md)) and wrong on npmjs.com, which cannot resolve a path; `fhevm-npm publish pack` is the only
producer of a tarball, and it renders every link per [NR-38](../entries/NR-38.md) into a staged copy before `npm pack`, so the tree is never
touched. `fhevm-npm publish check <payload>` reads the tarball with `tar` and fails on any surviving `file:` spec, a
version other than the central one, a dependency on another payload whose range is not what that payload's
central version renders to, or an entry point the shipped `package.json` declares (`main`, `module`,
`types`, `bin`, any `exports` leaf) that the tarball does not contain — `files` is a whitelist, so a built
entry point left out of it publishes a package that resolves to nothing, and the `publint`/`attw` gate of
[NR-61](../entries/NR-61.md) inspects the payload directory rather than this artifact. With `--check-npmjs` it also requires every rendered range to
have a published satisfying version — retried, because the previous release job publishes the dependency moments earlier
— and the payload's own version to be absent, never retried. `fhevm-npm publish order` derives a sequence from the
links. The release workflow writes a dependency order down by hand, as one job per payload, each waiting for the one
before; nothing checks it against `publish order`. In a real release the order is still enforced by refusal, since each
job's `publish check --check-npmjs` refuses a payload whose dependency is not on npmjs.com yet. Before the first job,
`fhevm-npm publish rehearse` packs every payload of the release set into the tarballs directory and checks them
together, in publish order, a dependency inside the set being satisfied by its freshly packed tarball, so a payload a
later job would refuse stops the release before anything is published; `make publish-rehearse` runs the same rehearsal
on a developer machine. `publish render <payload>` shows the same rendering without producing anything.

```sh
# ✅ Before any job publishes: the whole release set packed and checked together.
# The excluded payload key is illustrative.
fhevm-npm publish rehearse --exclude "./example-owner/pkg"

# ✅ Then one job per payload $p, in the workflow's dependency order, each payload proven just before it goes out.
tgz=$(fhevm-npm publish pack "$p")
fhevm-npm publish render "$p"
fhevm-npm publish check "$p" --check-npmjs
npm publish "$tgz"

# ❌ Publishes the working tree: the tarball ships "file:../../../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg".
npm publish ./hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg
```

Ordinary members have none (their installation root's lock
covers them); a standalone project keeps its own, and so does a non-member consumer registered in `consumerTests`,
because its isolated copy is an independent installation root. A workspace MEMBER registered as a consumer (a Hardhat
template) still has none: its installation root locks it, and `test-consumer` resolves its isolated copy fresh. Consumer
lockfiles are immutable except through `test-consumer-regenerate-package-lock`, which refuses a member.

```text
✅ ordinary workspace member                    <installation root>/package-lock.json only
✅ standalone consumer                         <consumer>/package-lock.json
✅ workspace member registered as a consumer   <installation root>/package-lock.json only (fresh isolated resolve)
❌ ordinary workspace member                    nested package-lock.json
```

`test-consumer` derives each consumer's install mode: it replays a committed lockfile with `npm ci --install-links`,
and runs `npm install --install-links` for a workspace member (none by policy) or for an isolated consumer that lacks
one, which prints a warning. `--ci` turns that warning into an error and changes nothing else.

<a id="nr-65"></a>

## NR-65: No extraneous lockfile nodes `[HOLD]`

> No lockfile carries an extraneous node.

Old number: 6.1.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check extraneous`

npm writes `"extraneous": true` on a package it knows about but
cannot reach from the declared graph — nothing in any `package.json` asks for it. It is what a RETARGETED dependency
leaves behind: the edges move to the new target, the old node is demoted rather than deleted, and the lockfile goes on
naming a package that is no longer in the tree. Retargeting the Hardhat plugins from `<vN-1>`'s payload to `<vN>`'s left
exactly that in three lockfiles at once.

npm will not install it, which is precisely why it survives: nothing breaks, so nobody notices. The cost is that the
lockfile stops being the record of what a clean machine gets, and the stale line reads like a real dependency to the
next person auditing it — a retired generation still apparently in the tree long after the switch. It outlives every
incremental install; only rebuilding the tree drops it.

```text
❌ "../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg": { "extraneous": true }   after the plugin moved to <vN>/pkg
✅ rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install               the node is gone, the edges stay
```

Both lockfile shapes are read — `packages` (lockfileVersion 2 and 3) and the legacy nested `dependencies` (version 1)
— so an older file cannot pass vacuously.

examples/standalone/package.json

# ✅ The validator identifies and excludes its own autonomous package tree.
<validator-installation>/package.json

# ✅ A separately managed tree is excluded explicitly, including all of its descendants.
"inventory": { "exclude": ["./separately-managed-sdk"] }

# ✅ Ignore rules exclude generated and installed trees without hard-coding their names here.
node_modules/dependency/package.json           # ignored dependency installation
cache/tool/package.json                        # ignored generated cache
tarballs/unpacked/package.json                 # ignored release output

# ✅ An explicit standalone entry includes its own ignored root manifest, but not its generated children.
examples/standalone/package.json               # included
examples/standalone/cache/package.json         # still ignored

# ❌ Discovering only workspace members misses valid non-member package.json files.
package.json -> workspaces[]

prune = ["node_modules", ".git"]

enforces safe lexical forms for every path field; the validator additionally resolves each local path against its
declared root, follows symlinks with `realpath`, and rejects a result outside that root.

```jsonc
// ✅ Canonical paths stay below their documented roots.
"publishedRelPath": "./hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg"
"source": "./common-vendored/src"

// ❌ Traversal is rejected even when normalization would produce an in-tree path.
"publishedRelPath": "./hardhat/v2/../v3/plugin/pkg"
"source": "./common-vendored/../outside"

// ❌ A vendored filename is one basename, not a path or traversal segment.
"files": ["..", "nested/file.ts"]
```

## NR-83: Each event links to the one before `[GAP]`

Old number: 8.3.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/deployments.ts:646-648` finds an attempt's target by exact path, so an attempt that links through a byte-identical copy in its own folder fails before the copy allowance runs. Fix: find the target by the copy's sha256 (issue I-59, decision D15).

Issues: I-10, I-59, I-68.

A deploy has no `previous`. Every other event's manifest has
`previous.path` resolving to the previous event's manifest, `previous.sha256` equal to that file's bytes, and
`previous.deploymentId`, `chainId`, `version`, `packageVersion` equal to it. An attempt links the same way to the event
it started from. The sha256 is the link and the path only says where those bytes are, so the path may instead resolve to
a copy of that manifest kept inside the event's own folder, provided its bytes are identical: what an operator's seal says
when `previousManifest` pointed at a copy. A seal is never rewritten ([NR-84](../entries/NR-84.md)), so such an event could not otherwise be
archived. Through such a copy, and only there, `previous.packageVersion` may be absent when the previous manifest has
none: the folder name that stands for it was out of the tool's sight.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

## NR-86: The developer moves the generations, and the checks only read `[GAP]`

> The developer creates the generation directories and edits every pin, and the checks only read them and report.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: no test runs the checks on a read-only copy of the workspace, so a check that writes into a generation directory or rewrites a pin would pass. `fhevm-npm check generations`, `check generation-parity`, and `check cleartext-config` only read today. Fix: a test that runs every check command and fails if the workspace changed.

A rotation is a change that a person reviews: a new `<vN>` directory, the `previous` and `current` entries of `npm-manifest.json#generations`, and every dependency spec that moves from `<vN-1>` to `<vN>`. The developer makes all of it, by hand or with a command written for that purpose, and the diff of the pull request shows each edit.

A check never makes any of it. It reads the workspace and reports what breaks a rule. If a check fixed a pin or moved a directory itself, the fix would land without review, and a wrong fix would hide the very problem the check exists to report.

#### Examples

- ✅ The developer adds `host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>`, moves `current` and `previous` in the manifest, and edits each pin. `fhevm-npm check generations` then reports every pin that still targets `<vN-1>`.
- ✅ A command made to write, such as `fhevm-npm generate cleartext-config`, writes its files when the developer runs it, and the developer commits the result.
- ❌ A check that finds a pin on `<vN-1>` and rewrites it to `<vN>` before it reports success.
- ❌ A check that creates a missing generation directory so that its own test passes.

`fhevm-npm check package-json` with its sort option is not an exception: it reorders the fields of a `package.json` only when the developer asks for it, and changes no value.

[WORKSPACE.md](../../WORKSPACE.md) explains how generations live side by side in the workspace. [ND-01](../../definitions/entries/ND-01.md) and [ND-02](../../definitions/entries/ND-02.md) define a generation family and a live generation.

<a id="nr-87"></a>

## NR-87: A family has exactly two live generations `[GAP]`

> A generation family always has two live generations, the current one and the previous one.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check json-schemas`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: on `release/0.14.x`, the schema of `npm-manifest.json` makes `previous` optional, so a family that names only `current` passes `fhevm-npm check json-schemas`. Fix: issue I-120 makes `previous` required; the change is ready, not committed, on `devex/alexb/v14/rule-coverage-checks`.

Issues: I-120, I-121.

`npm-manifest.json#generations` names, for each [generation family](../../definitions/entries/ND-01.md), its `current` generation, `<vN>`, and its `previous` generation, `<vN-1>`. These are its two [live generations](../../definitions/entries/ND-02.md). Both are always there: `previous` is the stack that the upgrade suite of `current` upgrades from. A family names no third generation: `<vN-2>` is retired once `<vN>` arrives.

The two live generations are two different dev packages, each in its own directory below the directory of the family.

#### The workspace runs ahead of the networks

The workspace rotates when the developer starts the next generation, not when a network deploys one. Work on a new generation often starts while the current one is not on testnet yet. The rotation then happens anyway: the new generation becomes `current`, the generation before it becomes `previous`, and the one before that is retired from the workspace, even if a network still runs it. So `current` can be a generation that no network runs yet.

#### Examples

```jsonc
// ✅ Two live generations.
"host-contracts-cleartext": {
  "current": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>",
  "previous": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>"
}

// ✅ Work on the next generation started while <vN> was not on testnet yet.
// The workspace rotated anyway: the new generation is current, and the
// generation before it is previous, although no network runs either yet.
"host-contracts-cleartext": {
  "current": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN+1>",
  "previous": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>"
}

// ❌ No previous generation. The upgrade suite of current has nothing to upgrade from.
"host-contracts-cleartext": { "current": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>" }

// ❌ A third generation. The manifest has no place for it, and the schema refuses any other key.
"host-contracts-cleartext": {
  "current": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>",
  "previous": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>",
  "older": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-2>"
}

// ❌ The same directory twice.
"host-contracts-cleartext": {
  "current": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>",
  "previous": "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>"
}
```

> **Implemented.** The schema of `npm-manifest.json`, which `fhevm-npm check json-schemas` applies, allows only the keys `current` and `previous` for each family, so a third generation fails. The TypeScript validator also requires both to be different dev packages, each below the directory of the family. Nothing requires `previous` yet on `release/0.14.x`: that is the gap, which issue I-120 closes.

[WORKSPACE.md](../../WORKSPACE.md) explains how generations live side by side in the workspace.

<a id="nr-88"></a>

## NR-88: The Hardhat 2 plugin's version constants follow their sources `[HOLD]`

> The two package versions that the Hardhat 2 plugin writes in `src/internal/constants.ts` equal their sources of truth.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli sync hh-v2-constants --check`

The Hardhat 2 plugin, `hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg`, hardcodes two package versions in `src/internal/constants.ts` and reads
them at run time:

- `FHEVM_HOST_CONTRACTS_CLEARTEXT_PACKAGE` equals the version that `versions.json` gives the host-contracts-cleartext
  payload, at the key the plugin's own `file:` dependency points to. The rule follows the plugin when it moves to
  another generation.
- `FHEVM_SOLIDITY_PACKAGE` equals the floor of the `@fhevm/solidity` spec in `npm-manifest.json#dependencies.pinned`:
  `^X.Y.Z` gives `X.Y.Z`, the release whose addresses the block was checked against.

Each block carries its version twice, in the comment above it and in its `version` field. Both equal the source.

`version apply` writes the derived versions of [NR-37](../entries/NR-37.md) and `sync pinned` writes the pins of
[NR-21](../entries/NR-21.md), but neither touches this file. Without this rule it drifts silently after a version bump or a pin
change, and the plugin then describes a package that the workspace no longer builds. The remedy is
`fhevm-npm sync hh-v2-constants`, which rewrites only those four spots. `--check` compares instead of writing, and runs
in `make check-pre`.

The rule applies to Hardhat 2 only. When `hardhat/v2` is deleted, retire this rule together with the command: the
header of `fhevm-npm/commands/sync-hh-v2-constants.ts` lists what goes.

```ts
// ✅ Both spots equal the source: versions.json gives the payload X.Y.Z.
// @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext@X.Y.Z
FHEVM_HOST_CONTRACTS_CLEARTEXT_PACKAGE: {
  version: 'X.Y.Z',

// ❌ The version moved in versions.json, and the constant still names the old release.
// @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext@X.Y.W
```

<a id="nr-89"></a>

## NR-89: Solhint has no place in the workspace `[HOLD]`

> Outside a mirror-only tree, no file configures, declares, installs, or names Solhint.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check lint-policy`

`forge lint` is the Solidity linter of the workspace, and `forge fmt` its formatter ([NR-44](../entries/NR-44.md)). A second
linter reports against rules that no script runs, and a directive written for it is dead text that a reader still has
to understand. So Solhint appears nowhere:

- No configuration file or folder whose name starts with `.solhint` or `solhint.config.`, anywhere in the workspace.
- No `package.json` that names it, in a dependency or in a script. [NR-20](../entries/NR-20.md) forbids the package itself; this
  also catches a script that calls it, and an alias that hides its name.
- No runnable `node_modules/.bin/solhint` in any installation root. No workspace package declares it, so an installed
  binary always means that something brought it in.
- No line that names it in the Solidity a Foundry dev package owns, such as a `// solhint-disable-next-line`
  directive.

Two trees are exempt. A mirror-only payload keeps the Solhint its upstream declares, because the published template
carries it ([NR-44](../entries/NR-44.md)). Vendored Solidity stays byte-identical to upstream ([NR-42a](../entries/NR-42a.md)), so a
directive in it stays too.

```solidity
// ✅ forge lint reads its own directive.
// forge-lint: disable-next-line(mixed-case-function)

// ❌ No script runs Solhint, so this line silences nothing.
// solhint-disable-next-line func-name-mixedcase
```

<a id="nr-90"></a>

## NR-90: Cleartext-config faces are generated, never edited `[HOLD]`

> Every face of `cleartext-config.json` equals what `fhevm-npm generate cleartext-config` renders from it.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check cleartext-config`

`cleartext-config.json` at the workspace root is the only source of a value that the languages of the cleartext stack
must agree on: a chain ID, a localhost address, a KMS node parameter. Each value is decided there once. The generator
renders it into three faces for every generation that `appliesTo.generations` lists ([NR-24](../entries/NR-24.md)):

- `common-vendored/src/cleartext-config-<gen>.ts`, the complete TypeScript face. `sync vendored` copies it into the
  payload as `pkg/ts/cleartext-config.ts` ([NR-23](../entries/NR-23.md)).
- `host-contracts-cleartext/<gen>/pkg/src/cleartext/shared/LibFhevmCleartextConfig.sol`, the Solidity face.
- `host-contracts-cleartext/<gen>/scripts/cleartext-config.sh`, the shell face that the launchers source.

A face is never edited, not even a comment in it: the comments come from the `summary` and `note` of each value in
the JSON. A hand edit makes one language disagree with the others, or is lost at the next `make generate`. To change a
value or its text, edit the JSON and run `fhevm-npm generate cleartext-config` (a step of `make generate`). A missing
face fails the check as well as a face that differs.

```sh
# ✅ The JSON changes, and every face follows.
$EDITOR cleartext-config.json && ./fhevm-npm-cli generate cleartext-config && ./fhevm-npm-cli sync vendored

# ❌ One face now disagrees with the JSON and with the other two.
$EDITOR host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/src/cleartext/shared/LibFhevmCleartextConfig.sol
```
